correctness.rationale: For \(x=(a,v,c)\) and \(y=(d,w,f)\), direct multiplication gives the commutator \((0,(a-c)w-(d-f)v,0)\). This single equation determines the center, all centralizers, and every commutator fiber. The centralizer classification splits into central elements, nonzero radical elements, and elements with unequal diagonal coordinates. The zero-fiber count and each nonzero-fiber count sum exactly to \(|A_{r,q}|^2\). The divisor-family collision follows algebraically from \(q^r=p^M\) and strict monotonicity in the field exponent. The packaged exhaustive checker independently verifies multiplication, centralizers, fibers, and probabilities in seven cases.

originality.rationale: The closest same-invariant source studies finite rings through their number of centralizers, gives a prime rank-two family, and computes several small-centralizer cases. Its explicit six-centralizer probability calculation excludes the elementary-abelian rank-four central factor. The final theorem gives a uniform path-algebra family with exact centralizer geometry and all commutator fibers; its \(A_{1,4}\) specialization produces probability \(19/64\) in that excluded central-factor case. Targeted database and web searches found no equivalent generalized-Kronecker formula or the \(19/64\) six-centralizer specialization.

value.rationale: The result connects a standard representation-theoretic path-algebra family to the finite-ring centralizer/commuting-probability program. It gives more than a single probability: every element-centralizer and every commutator fiber is explicit. The divisor construction shows systematically that centralizer count alone does not determine commuting probability, and the \(A_{1,4}\) case supplies an exact probability in a central-factor case explicitly omitted from the closest published six-centralizer calculation. These are structural consequences that remain meaningful beyond the checked finite examples.
